_comment: Inputs to scripts/classify_weights.py. Every entry here is checkable by opening a URL. Nothing is classified from memory.

hf_namespaces._comment: OpenRouter organisation prefix -> Hugging Face namespace. Verify any entry at https://huggingface.co/<namespace>. The classifier confirms each namespace actually publishes weight repos before it trusts a negative result from it, so a wrong entry here degrades to unclassified rather than to a false closed.

closed_weight_orgs._comment: Organisations that serve their models without publishing weights at all. A model from one of these is closed unless OpenRouter itself gives it a hugging_face_id, which is what keeps openai/gpt-oss and google/gemma on the open side. Checkable by the absence of a weights repo under the organisation's own namespace.

tiers._comment: Capability tiers from benchmarks.artificial_analysis.intelligence_index in the OpenRouter payload. Bands are absolute and fixed, NOT percentiles of the current snapshot, so a model's tier does not change because other models were added or removed. Chosen on 2026-10-30 at the two widest gaps in that day's distribution (nothing scored 40.0-44.9, and the 20-24 band held two models). They are frozen: re-tuning bands after seeing a result is how a comparison gets talked into saying what you wanted.
tiers.source: Artificial Analysis intelligence index v5, from the AA data API, joined by scripts/aa_match.py. Where AA scores several reasoning configurations for one model, the highest is used.
tiers._rebase_note: The band boundaries are unchanged from when they were frozen on 2026-10-30. Only the score source moved, from the thin slice OpenRouter embedded in its payload to the full AA v5 index collected directly. See docs/decisions.md, 2026-11-04.

blend._comment: Input-to-output token ratio for the blended price. blended = (R * input_price + output_price) / (R + 1), a price per million tokens of mixed traffic at R input tokens per output token. There is no public token mix for the OpenRouter catalogue, so R is an assumption, not a measurement. The base of 5:1 is a mid estimate for chat and agentic traffic, where prompts and retrieved context outweigh generated text. The sensitivity ratios bracket it: 1:1 for generation-heavy work such as translation or drafting, 20:1 for retrieval and long-context agentic work. Every published figure must name the ratio it used.

_file_note: Inputs for the analysis scripts: weight classification, capability tiers and the price blend. The file name predates the last two sections.
